details.description: Linden 1 is Speechmatics' speech-to-text model built specifically for Agent STT, its turn-based transcription service for voice agents, reached over a dedicated /v2/agent WebSocket endpoint; Speechmatics states Agent STT is powered by linden-1 and offers no alternative model. Rather than a running word stream, it returns speaker-attributed, punctuated segments together with explicit start-of-turn and end-of-turn signals, formatted to pass directly to an LLM. Speechmatics states Agent STT is available in 55+ languages and, as of its current documentation, on SaaS only.
advantages: Returns speaker-attributed, punctuated transcript segments with explicit turn-start and turn-end signals rather than a raw word stream, formatted to pass directly to an LLM, per Speechmatics' Agent STT documentation.
Speechmatics states end-of-speech finalization lands in about 350ms, per Speechmatics' Voice Agents page.
Includes speaker diarization by default, attributing every word to the speaker who said it, per Speechmatics' Voice Agents page.
Supports a custom vocabulary of up to 1,000 domain-specific terms, per Speechmatics' Voice Agents page.
Speechmatics states Agent STT is available in 55+ languages, per Speechmatics' Voice Agents page.
Integrates directly with the Vapi, LiveKit and Pipecat voice-agent platforms, plus a Python SDK and a direct WebSocket API for any other language, per Speechmatics' Agent STT documentation.
disadvantages: Agent STT, the product linden-1 powers, is available on SaaS only, per Speechmatics' Agent STT documentation.
Linden 1 is the only model Agent STT offers, so there is no alternative model to choose for this endpoint.
use_cases: Building voice AI agents for conversational, LLM-driven applications
Real-time, multi-speaker call or meeting transcription feeding directly into an LLM
Customer-facing voice bots built on Vapi, LiveKit or Pipecat

sources.title: Agent STT WebSocket API - Speechmatics Documentation

notes: No page states a deprecation, beta or preview flag for linden-1 itself; Agent STT's own documentation says the product is 'on SaaS only' (no self-hosted/on-prem deployment mentioned), which is noted as a limitation. The Agent STT documentation page states 'The Agent STT SDK is a Python client for the Agent STT service'; it does not mention a JavaScript or .NET SDK for Agent STT specifically (those exist for Speechmatics' general Realtime API, not confirmed for the /v2/agent endpoint), so the SDK claim was corrected. The Languages reference page states Linden 1 'supports the same languages as Realtime transcription' and gives no separate count for it; that page's Realtime/Batch-shared list of 55 individually-named languages (excluding 'Automatic' and the bilingual/multi-language packs, which have no per-language breakdown of Realtime support) is used here. Catalog carries no deprecation_date.
